title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue of Beihai Maritime Court Formally Accepting Cases
keywords_en: Maritime Court formally accepts cases for filing
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on the Issue of Beihai Maritime Court Formally Accepting Cases

Fa [1999] No. 123

All High People's Courts of Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and all Maritime Courts:

In accordance with the spirit of the Supreme People's Court's Approval on the Establishment of Beihai Maritime Court in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, we hereby notify the following issues regarding the formal acceptance of cases by Beihai Maritime Court:

1. Beihai Maritime Court has jurisdiction over first-instance maritime and maritime commerce cases arising in the ports and waters belonging to Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, as well as in the Beibu Gulf waters, its islands, and waters therein. The boundary between its jurisdiction and that of Guangzhou Maritime Court shall be the center line of the Yingluo Bay river channel. Areas to the east of the center line of the river channel and its extended waters shall be under the jurisdiction of Guangzhou Maritime Court; areas to the west of the center line of the river channel and its extended waters, including Wuni Island, Weizhou Island, and Xieyang Island, shall be under the jurisdiction of Beihai Maritime Court. Appellate cases against first-instance judgments of Beihai Maritime Court shall be under the jurisdiction of the High People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

2. The scope of cases accepted by Beihai Maritime Court shall be handled in accordance with the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Scope of Cases Accepted by Maritime Courts.

3. The management of personnel, finances, and property of Beihai Maritime Court shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Opinions on Certain Issues Concerning the Streamlining of the Management System of Six Maritime Courts Including Dalian (Zhong Bian Ban Fa [1999] No. 5).

4. Beihai Maritime Court shall formally commence operations and accept cases on July 1, 1999.

After July 1, 1999, Guangzhou Maritime Court shall no longer accept maritime and maritime commerce cases within the aforementioned jurisdiction. Cases already accepted before that date shall not be transferred, and their appellate cases shall still be tried by the High People's Court of Guangdong Province.

July 19, 1999
